title: Condensation for the constructible hierarchy
summary: Identify transitive models of a fixed construction fragment and V=L as constructible levels, then preserve named subsets through elementary collapses.
abstract: Collapsing a well-founded membership relation produces a transitive set, but it does not by itself identify which transitive set appears. The constructible hierarchy gives a sharper answer when the starting structure can carry out its own level construction and believes that every set is constructible. We prove that such a transitive structure is exactly the level at its ordinal height. An elementary submodel of a sufficiently strong constructible level inherits these hypotheses, so its collapse is another constructible level. We then show how to choose a small hull retaining every point of an infinite ordinal and a chosen subset, and why its collapse leaves that subset unchanged.
